title: Reflexive verbs
tagline: I get up, I get dressed: conjugation, verbs that are reflexive only in French and the past with être.
goal: Describe your routine, conjugate verbs with se and use them in the negative, the imperative and the passé composé.

blocks.text: It's a verb used with a reflexive pronoun (*me, te, se…*), like «myself», «yourself» in English. The difference is that French uses them **far more often**, including where English uses «get» or no pronoun at all.
Before a vowel or silent h, *me, te, se* → *m', t', s'*. Hence *je m'appelle* (my name is). And *nous nous* or *vous vous* aren't a typo: the first is the subject, the second the reflexive.

Almost every routine verb is reflexive in French: *se réveiller* (to wake up), *se lever* (to get up), *se doucher* (to have a shower), *s'habiller* (to get dressed), *se coucher* (to go to bed). **If English says «get…» or «wake up», French often uses a reflexive.**

blocks.title: Se lever
blocks.text: It takes a grave accent in the forms with a silent ending: *je me lève, tu te lèves, il se lève, ils se lèvent* (but *nous nous levons, vous vous levez*).

blocks.title: Body parts
blocks.text: French uses the article, not the possessive: «I brush my teeth» = *Je me brosse {les} dents* (not «mes dents»).

sections.title: Where French and English don't match

head: Case
Examples
rows: Reflexive in French, not in English
to remember → *se souvenir de* · to go for a walk → *se promener* · to rest → *se reposer* · to hurry → *se dépêcher* · to sit down → *s'asseoir*
*appeler* (to call) → *s'appeler* (to be called) · *ennuyer* (to bore someone) → *s'ennuyer* (to be bored) · *tromper* (to cheat on) → *se tromper* (to be wrong)

blocks.text: *Je me suis trompé* = I made a mistake. *Je t'ai trompé* = I cheated on you. Best not to mix them up.

blocks.title: Each other
blocks.text: Reflexive verbs also mean «each other»: *Ils s'aiment* (they love each other) · *Nous nous parlons tous les jours* (we talk to each other every day) · *Elles se téléphonent* (they call each other).

head: Situation
Rule
Example
rows: the reflexive stays next to the verb
the reflexive goes with the infinitive and matches the subject
*Je vais me coucher. · Tu vas te coucher.*

sections.title: In the passé composé, always with être

blocks.text: Every reflexive verb uses **être** in the past [[10]], so the participle agrees with the subject:
**Negative in the past:** *Je ne me suis pas réveillé(e).*

exercises.instructions: Translate into French. Careful: it doesn't always match English.

items.answer: Nous nous promenons dans le parc.
accept: On se promène dans le parc.

exercises.instructions: Write the sentence in the negative.

items.answer: Je ne me lève pas tôt.

items.prompt: (to your group, including you) Let's hurry.

exercises.title: Yesterday morning
exercises.instructions: Conjugate in the passé composé. Watch the agreement.

items.prompt: Hier matin, Julie ___ à 6 h. (se réveiller)
Ses frères, eux, ___ à 9 h ! (se lever)
Le soir, ils ___ très tard. (se coucher)

checklist: I conjugate reflexive verbs in the present.
I can describe my daily routine.
I use them in the negative and the imperative.
I use them in the passé composé with *être*.
I know the verbs that are reflexive only in French (*se souvenir, se promener, se dépêcher*).

challenge.title: Your routine
challenge.text: Describe this morning in the present with six reflexive verbs, then tell it in the past: *Je me suis réveillé(e) à 7 h, je me suis douché(e)…*
